rationale: CONCLUSION: compliant at the preferred position; no redline. CUSTOMER CONVENIENCE TERMINATION IS PRESENT, in Section 14 (p0079), quoted above. Client may end this Agreement on written notice of its "election to terminate" alone: the right is unconditional and requires no cause, breach, default, or TrueLink consent, and no early-termination fee, penalty, liquidated damages or other exit charge appears anywhere in the reviewed text. The sole consequence of Client's notice is that services run to the last day of the following month, an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, which sits at the preferred 30-day position and comfortably inside the 60-90 day fallback. VENDOR HAS NO MID-TERM CONVENIENCE EXIT. Section 13 (p0078) fixes a one-year term with automatic one-year renewals; TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off is the automatic partial termination of Sections 2 and 3, which is cause-based (Client act/omission causing a TrueLink breach under a System or Credit Repository Agreement, or Client breach of Sections 8a-8c). Neither walk-away trigger is engaged: there is no Vendor convenience right on under 90 days' notice, and the 12-month term defeats the "no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term" trigger in any event. WHY THE DETERMINISTIC "CONVENIENCE TERMINATION PRESENT" CHECK CANNOT PASS: the check looks for express convenience-termination wording, and no such wording exists anywhere in this document to quote. A full-text search shows "for convenience" appears only in Section 22 captions boilerplate (p0088, "included for convenience of reference only"), and "may terminate" and "without cause" appear nowhere; the only hit for termination-election language is p0079. The right is drafted obliquely, as TrueLink's continuing service obligation up to the Client-elected termination date, rather than as an express "Client may terminate for convenience" grant. This is a phrasing variant, not a substantive gap, so the heuristic miss is unresolvable by quote selection and does not change the classification. MINOR SHORTFALLS, NOTED NOT REDLINED, per the playbook's treatment of sub-elements: (1) no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, largely moot because Section 5a (p0045) invoices Hosting and Support Services monthly with payment due 15 days after receipt, so fees run in arrears and little or nothing is prepaid; (2) the Section 13 non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than 90, but it is mutual, operates only at natural expiry rather than as a mid-term exit, and tightening TrueLink's side would equally cut back our own flexibility, so flagging it would work against our party. OPEN ITEM FOR CONFIRMATION, not asserted as a breach: Section 14 opens "Subject to Section 4 hereof" and Section 4 is not in the reviewed text. The cross-references in Section 6 (p0047) indicate Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees; if Section 4 in fact preserves minimum monthly fees after termination or otherwise conditions Client's right, it could operate as a de facto exit charge and this rule should be reopened.

Vendor-side risk is correctly analysed: Section 13 sets a 1-year term with 1-year renewals and TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off (partial termination of Sections 2-3) is cause-based, so neither walk-away trigger (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term; Vendor convenience on <90 days) is engaged. The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is adequately explained as a phrasing artefact - the right is drafted obliquely as TrueLink's continuing obligation up to the Client-elected termination date rather than as express 'terminate for convenience' wording - so the regex miss is evidence of a variant, not a substantive gap. Sub-elements short of the preferred position (no express pro-rata refund, monthly arrears billing making prepayment largely moot, 30-day mutual non-renewal notice) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements, and tightening the mutual non-renewal notice would cut against our own flexibility. The unresolved 'Subject to Section 4' cross-reference (potential minimum-monthly-fee tail) is flagged as an open item for confirmation rather than asserted as a breach, which is an appropriate hedge and does not undermine the compliant classification on the reviewed text.

quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against Mortgage Logic.com anywhere in the Agreement. Sections 2-4 (license/services), 5-6 (compensation), 7 (spamming), 8 (Client covenants) and 10 (confidentiality) were read in full, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "examine", "verif", "monitor" and "premises" returned no hits. The verification-type mechanics that exist run in our favour: §6 entitles us to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them, and §3(e) gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. The nearest TrueLink-side rights are §8(f) (TrueLink may implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming) and §9 (we give reasonable access so TrueLink can make Y2K repairs and upgrades at its sole cost); both are narrow, self-funded Vendor rights rather than audits of our usage, and neither creates frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure. AUDIT is a protective rule that caps Vendor audits of us, so silence is at least as favourable as the preferred position: proposing frequency/notice/cost parameters would gratuitously create an audit right TrueLink does not have. That is why this is compliant rather than "missing" - the playbook directs us not to flag what benefits our party. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency limit; it is a heuristic artefact and no unaddressed risk remains. If TrueLink later seeks a usage-audit right, we would require the preferred terms (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to our systems), with the fallback at once per year on 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold.

verification.notes: audit frequency limited: failed Claimed status is compliant and consistent with the artifacts: no redline and no counterparty comment were produced, so nothing is being raised as a negotiation issue. The cited paragraphs support the rationale — §6 (documentation on request) and §3(e) (real-time usage statistics/log access) run in Customer's favour, and §8(f) is a narrow anti-spamming technical-measures right, not a usage audit with frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure. AUDIT is a protective cap on Vendor audit rights; silence is at least as favourable as the preferred position, so inserting audit parameters would gratuitously create a right TrueLink does not have. Treating this as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct under the instruction not to flag terms benefiting our party. The failed 'audit frequency limited' regex is explained as a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause to carry a frequency limit; no unaddressed risk is left open, and the rationale records the preferred/fallback parameters to demand if TrueLink later seeks an audit right.

quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance, including technology errors and omissions, of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. TrueLink shall provide Client with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry standard insurance (CGL, E&O and cyber) with certificates on request.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13-30 in sec-12) contain no coverage requirement, so the agreement lacks any insurance obligation. TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data and provides Support Services, which places the absence of coverage in walk-away territory under the rule (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data). We inserted a new Section 31 after Force Majeure (p0097) at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O (including tech E&O) USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request — and flagged the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the comment. Note the survival clause (p0090) references "Sections 1 and 5 through 30"; a conforming update to that cross-reference can be handled administratively.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The only pricing-parity language in the Agreement runs in our favour: § 6 (p0047) obliges TrueLink to hold Hosting Services costs flat for one year and to charge us rates no higher than it charges any other party. Nothing in the Compensation section, the Client covenants (§ 8) or elsewhere requires Mortgage Logic.com to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers (searches for "most favored", "no less favorable", "favorable", "any other party" and "rates" return no Customer-side parity undertaking). This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation on Customer, with a Vendor-granted MFN we retain — so no redline is proposed.

verification.notes: The cited § 6 language grants the MFN to Client (TrueLink's rates for Hosting Services 'will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party'), i.e., parity runs in our favour, which matches the rule's preferred position of no MFN obligation on Customer. No Customer-side obligation to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers appears in the supplied text, supporting the 'compliant' classification. quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly commitment on us (a floor for Hosting Services and for Support Services payable irrespective of actual usage), so this is not the preferred position of usage-only/ordered-services-only fees. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined: (i) the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term, because Section 13 (p0078) runs for one year and renews only in successive one-year periods with a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party; (ii) Section 14 (p0079) gives us a unilateral at-will termination right, with services and the corresponding minimum continuing only until the last day of the month following the month of our notice - an exit stronger than a mere volume reduction on 30 days' notice; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the agreement, so terminating simply stops the minimum prospectively, which operates as a true-up rather than a penalty. This is well clear of the walk-away case of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Two drafting points noted but not flagged as deviations under this rule: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank ($____) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges, which is a billing-transparency point better addressed under the audit/disputes rule. The "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in Section 4 (p0043) is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour, so it is not flagged.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and the redline is identical to the original text with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding. The cited clauses support the fallback: Section 5(a) imposes a monthly minimum, but Section 13 caps the term at one year with successive one-year renewals and a 30-day non-renewal right, and Section 14 lets Client terminate at will with the minimum ceasing at the end of the month following notice. No shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums appears in the cited text, so the exit operates prospectively rather than as a penalty — consistent with the fallback's true-up requirement and well clear of the multi-year take-or-pay walk-away. The rationale correctly notes it sits at the fallback rather than preferred, and correctly declines to flag the programmer-availability commitment, which runs in our favour, and defers the billing-transparency carve-out in Section 6 to the audit/disputes rule (no double-flagging). Blank dollar figures are appropriately noted as a drafting point rather than escalated as a deviation under this presence rule.

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale: Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) terms, with either party — including us as Client — able to prevent renewal on written notice given only 30 days before the end of the then-current year. That meets the preferred position on the material terms: 12-month renewal length and a 30-day customer opt-out, well inside the fallback's 60-day ceiling and far from the 90-day/multi-year walk-away. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal drafting and are noted rather than flagged: there is no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and there is no CPI/3% cap on renewal pricing (Section 6 (p0047) only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds a most-favoured-rate commitment, so post-year-one uplifts are uncapped). Per the playbook's classification semantics these are not independent deviations; we can raise the reminder and uplift cap as goodwill asks if the renewal economics are negotiated.

verification.notes: Cited Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year terms — not multi-year — with either party, including Client, able to block renewal on written notice given 30 days before the end of the then-current year. That satisfies the preferred position's material terms (12-month renewal, ≤30-day customer opt-out) and is well inside the 60-day fallback ceiling and far from the 90-day/multi-year walk-away. The claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistent with that, no redline was applied (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was generated — appropriate treatment for a clause retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue. The failed deterministic check ('non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days — number not found') is a phrasing artifact: the clause spells the window as 'thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year', which the regex did not capture. Substance clearly meets the threshold. The two shortfalls the rationale flags — no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal and no CPI/3% (or ≤5%) cap on post-year-one uplifts (Section 6 only freezes Hosting Services costs for one year plus a most-favoured-rate commitment) — are exactly the kind of minor sub-elements (missing reminder mechanic, missing price-uplift cap) the playbook directs be noted in the rationale rather than raised as independent deviations. Correctly handled and accurately described.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit provision to Section 14: on expiry or termination TrueLink provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement currently requires us to arrange a new hosting environment within 60 days but gives us no right to our own data or migration help, which is unworkable for borrower and loan data. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Client data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition or data-return provision. Section 14 (Termination) only fixes the date services stop; Section 13 places the burden on Client to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, without any TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy mechanic, and Section 2(f) (backups) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing in the document reaches even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days). Inserted the preferred language after Section 14 — six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification (with a carve-out for legally required retention). The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: The cited paragraphs (Section 13 term/discontinuation and Section 14 termination) contain no transition-assistance, data-return, export-format or deletion-certification mechanic; Section 13 only obliges Client to arrange a replacement name server/hosting environment and confirms ownership of domains and Client Content, which is not a return right. A 'missing' classification is therefore supportable for a hosting agreement. The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language closely (six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification) and is correctly localized to the parties and the actual data categories (Client Content, Credit Data, other Client data). The legal-retention carve-out is a reasonable, non-prejudicial addition. The edit is an insertion only \u2014 the existing Section 14 text is untouched \u2014 so it is the smallest change that reaches the preferred position; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and data-return/transition language is present. The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains what changed and why (60-day rehosting duty with no data-return right), cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Y2K warranty, so TrueLink stands behind nothing about how the Interface or the Hosting and Support Services actually perform. We have added our standard performance and conformance warranty (12 months for software, professional and workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair, replace or refund remedy; we can discuss a 90-day software / 30-day services period as a fallback.

ops.text: TrueLink further represents and warrants that (i) the Hosting Services, Support Services and any other agreed-upon services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (ii) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications; (iii) the Interface and all related software, as delivered by TrueLink, will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code; and (iv) TrueLink will comply in all material respects with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. Client's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services, Interface or software.

proposal.summary: Add TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy to Section 9

quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no warranty that the Interface or software conforms to its documentation, no professional/workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's "same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" is a self-referential standard of care, not a conformance warranty with a remedy, and the disclaimer at p0076 (while carving out express warranties) leaves nothing meaningful behind. This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so we insert an express performance and conformance warranty at the preferred position (12 months software, workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair, replace or refund remedy, noting the fallback period is negotiable.

checks.name: warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years

verification.notes: The document contains only a narrow Y2K warranty (Section 9) and a self-referential standard of care (Section 11) — neither provides a conformance warranty, workmanlike-services warranty, or any repair/replace/refund/re-performance remedy, so the clause fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies); 'deviation' with an insert is the correct classification per the detection guidance. The redline is appended to the existing 'TrueLink Warranties' section, which is the natural home, and tracks the model language closely (workmanlike services, conformance to documentation, no malicious code, compliance with laws, vendor-elected repair/replace/refund) without disturbing the surrounding text. No double-flagging or over-reach: the disclaimer at p0076 already carves out express warranties, so no edit to the disclaimer was needed, and the finding correctly leaves it alone. Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90/30-day fallback; the 12-month software period sits at the preferred position, which is appropriate for a genuine deviation. Deterministic checks pass and the changed-character volume is justified because the clause had to be inserted wholesale rather than tweaked.
